def test_below_threshold():
    # All elements below threshold
    assert below_threshold([1, 2, 3, 4], 5) == True
    assert below_threshold([1, 2, 3], 4) == True

    # Element equal to threshold (should return False)
    assert below_threshold([1, 2, 3], 3) == False

    # Element above threshold (should return False)
    assert below_threshold([1, 2, 10], 5) == False
    assert below_threshold([5, 1, 2], 3) == False

    # Empty list (vacuously true)
    assert below_threshold([], 0) == True
    assert below_threshold([], 100) == True

    # Single element cases
    assert below_threshold([1], 2) == True
    assert below_threshold([2], 2) == False
    assert below_threshold([3], 2) == False

    # Negative numbers
    assert below_threshold([-5, -1, 0], 1) == True
    assert below_threshold([-5, 0, 1], 1) == False
    assert below_threshold([-1, -2, -3], -1) == False

    # Threshold is zero
    assert below_threshold([-3, -1], 0) == True
    assert below_threshold([0, -1], 0) == False

    # All elements equal and below
    assert below_threshold([2, 2, 2], 3) == True

    # Large numbers
    assert below_threshold([10**6], 10**6 + 1) == True
    assert below_threshold([10**6], 10**6) == False

    # First element fails immediately
    assert below_threshold([100, 1, 2], 50) == False

    # Last element fails
    assert below_threshold([1, 2, 100], 50) == False

    print("All tests passed!")


# Run the tests
if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_below_threshold()
